root_cause: rich.markup.escape() only doubled backslashes that sat directly before something that looks like a tag (regex (\\*)(\[[a-z#/@][^[]*?]) ). A backslash at the very END of the string was left alone. When the escaped value is then put inside markup, as in f"[red]{escape('C:\\')}[/red]", that trailing backslash ends up right before [/red] and escapes the closing tag. The result renders as 'C:[/red]' instead of 'C:\' in red.
best_solution: In rich/markup.py::escape, after the existing _escape(escape_backslashes, markup) substitution, add `if markup.endswith("\\") and not markup.endswith("\\\\"): return markup + "\\"`. This doubles a lone trailing backslash, so a tag placed right after the escaped text sees an even number of backslashes. The renderer already reads '\\\\[tag]' as one literal backslash followed by a real tag. Reasoning from the title alone: 'escaping' points to the public escape() helper in markup.py. 'Trailing backslash' means the helper's output must survive having markup appended after it. So fix the producer (escape), not the parser (render). Test the round trip: Text.from_markup(f'[red]{escape(v)}[/red]').plain == v.
acceptable_alternatives: The odd-count trailing-backslash regex from the issue, (?<![\\])(?:[\\][\\])*[\\]$ followed by appending one backslash, is more general and also passes. Any change inside escape() works as long as escape('C:\\') returns 'C:\\\\' and existing escape/render tests keep passing. Patching render() does NOT work, because the test checks escape()'s output string directly.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_markup.py::test_escape_backslash_end: escape('C:\\') == 'C:\\\\' (one backslash in, two out); f'[red]{escape(value)}[/red]' == '[red]C:\\\\[/red]'; Text.from_markup(that).plain == 'C:\\' and .spans == [Span(0, 3, 'red')]. Existing test_render_escape and test_escape must still pass, so render() semantics cannot change.
locating_signals: The statement is a title plus an issue link: 'Fix escaping trailing backslash'. The word 'escaping' plus a grep for `def escape` leads straight to rich/markup.py::escape. The function is not named, but the verb in the title is its name. The issue text (not shown to the agent) has the exact repro, C:\ followed by [/red].
our_outcome_summary: Kaggle env: v4 PASS, v6/v7/v8 FAIL. v4 (285s, 108 calls) made the gold fix: appended a backslash in escape() when the string ends in exactly one backslash. It also changed the regex quantifier to lazy (\\*?), which is harmless, and left a lot of rambling comments. v6 changed no source at all, only an empty fix.diff and a verify_fix.py script, so escape('C:\\') still returned 'C:\\'. v7 fixed the wrong side: it patched render() to collapse trailing double backslashes in plain text. escape() stayed unchanged (test fails) and the existing test_render_escape broke (2 failed). v8 edited an unrelated file, rich/pretty.py (rstrip('\n') -> removesuffix, which also needs Python 3.9+), and added its own test file. It never touched escape().
generalizable_lesson: When a bug is about escaping, quoting or serializing, fix the producer (the escape() helper) so its output round-trips through the existing parser. Do not change the parser, because existing parser tests pin its behavior. Check with the round trip parse(wrap(escape(x))) == x, including x ending in the escape character. Also gate the final diff: it must change a non-test source file that the statement's key word points to (here 'escaping' -> def escape). A diff with only scratch scripts, or edits in an unrelated module, should be rejected before submitting.
